analysis.title: SanDisk Corp. (SNDK): Tight supply/demand conditions drive estimates as datacenter exposure moves higher
key_insights: GS expects SNDK to trade modestly higher after a quarter with guidance above the Street on revenue and EPS. Expectations were balanced going in, after strong memory-peer prints and a ~20% stock pullback over 30 days.

Datacenter was 43.5% of FY1Q27 revenue (nearly 45% per GS) with multiple eSSD wins at hyperscalers. Management says datacenter is roughly half of industry bit demand, up from ~20% in 2020, and expects the revenue mix to shift further toward it.

Management attributes datacenter growth to KV cache (longer prompts and larger context windows). It expects KV cache to be ~35% of the AI datacenter NAND market by 2030 and datacenter to exceed 55% of the NAND market in CY27.
SNDK repurchased another $5.0bn of stock in the quarter, $9.5bn to date, with $10.5bn left on the $20bn authorization. GS expects buybacks to step up.
SNDK announced an 8:1 stock split effective November 20, 2026.

SNDK closed two previously announced long-term supply agreements (NBMs) in the quarter, for 10 agreements with 8 unique customers, including multiple US hyperscalers. Customers that underestimated NAND needs have asked for more volume or extensions, and the added bits will be priced higher.

The NBMs cover ~50% of planned FY27 bit capacity and 65% of planned FY28 bit capacity (both unchanged), with $94bn total contract value at contracted floor prices (unchanged) and $16.5bn of guarantees (unchanged).
FQ3 revenue was $11.03bn, in line with GS at $11.22bn and above the Street at $10.74bn. Gross margin was 85.1% vs GS 85.7% and Street 84.9%. Non-GAAP EPS was $49.51 vs GS $49.80 and Street $46.73.

4Q guidance midpoint: revenue $12.4bn (GS $13.55bn, Street $12.08bn), gross margin 85.0% (GS 85.6%, Street 84.7%), non-GAAP EPS $55.00-$57.00, midpoint $56.00 (GS $59.71, Street $52.94). Guidance is above the Street and below GS.

GS raises CY26/CY27/CY28 EPS estimates by ~7% on average: CY26 $172.37 (+0.1%), CY27 $280.00 (+7.2%), CY28 $350.00 (+15.5%). CY27 gross margin rises 187 bps to 84.1% and CY28 gross margin rises 275 bps to 82.5%.
GS maintains Buy and cuts the 12-month target to $2,000 from $2,200, using 18x P/E (from 20x, on lower peer multiples) on unchanged normalized EPS of $110. Price is $1,330.05, implying 50.4% upside.
GS expects a neutral reaction for MU (Neutral) given similar end-market exposures.
GS's thesis is that NAND supply additions will be very limited for the foreseeable future and SNDK's product portfolio and mix keep improving.

market_movers.rationale: Buy maintained on limited NAND supply additions and improving mix. The target is cut from $2,200 to $2,000 because the P/E multiple falls to 18x from 20x on lower peer multiples.
GS expects a neutral reaction in MU to SNDK's results given similar end-market exposures.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees very limited NAND supply additions for the foreseeable future, with datacenter demand rising on AI and KV cache needs.

earnings_insights: SNDK FQ3'26 (reported 10/29, quarter ended 9/26): revenue $11.03bn reported vs GS est $11.22bn and Street (Visible Alpha) est $10.74bn. Revenue was +23.0% QoQ and +377.9% YoY.
SNDK FQ3'26 non-GAAP EPS $49.51 reported vs GS est $49.80 and Street est $46.73. Gross margin was 85.1% and operating margin 80.4% (Street est 79.1%).

SNDK 4Q26 guidance (company): revenue $12.2-12.6bn, midpoint $12.4bn vs GS est $13.55bn and Street est $12.08bn. Non-GAAP EPS $55.00-$57.00 vs GS est $59.71 and Street est $52.94. Gross margin guided to 84.5-85.5%.
Datacenter was 43.5% of FY1Q27 revenue, and management expects the mix to shift further toward it.
SNDK bought back $5.0bn of stock in the quarter ($9.5bn to date), with $10.5bn of the $20bn authorization remaining.

trade_ideas.description: Long SNDK (Buy), 12-month target $2,000 on 18x P/E applied to normalized EPS of $110
trade_ideas.rationale: Limited NAND supply additions, rising datacenter and eSSD traction, long-term supply agreements and rising buybacks.
trade_ideas.risk: NAND pricing structural change fails to materialize; YMTC keeps iterating on its roadmap; SanDisk fails to gain eSSD traction.

risk_factors: Long-term structural change in NAND pricing fails to materialize.
YMTC continues to iterate on its roadmap.
SanDisk fails to gain eSSD traction.
GS bear case: 5x P/E on $88 EPS gives $440, -66.9% downside.
